body:
Hmm doesn't happen for me. Have you given it all permissions (including all the individual health permissions)? And to confirm, you are on 2.6.11b?

And do you have any logs from the crash?

I tap the icon; the app tries to open but then closes automatically. It doesn't even get to the point of asking for permissions. It works fine on Android 16. I don't have any logs - I am not an advanced user.

Yes, it’s the latest version, but I’ve had this issue for the last few versions. I don’t even remember which one it was that worked fine...

@tmpjx555 If you're willing:
1. Install Shizuku and follow setup steps in the app
2. Install aShell and grant the app Shizuku permission
3. Review the following command before running
4. logcat -b crash --pid=$(pidof com.vayunmathur.health)
5. Start the Health app

Make sure to stop the Shizuku service after getting the logs. 

While Shizuku and aShell aren't malicious, Shizuku is a security risk because it has the permission of the Shell app. 

Shell is an app with system-level permissions.

Probably follow @vayun-mathur 's instructions below before trying this, if it's unsuccessful try getting logs.

@tmpjx555 Given it happened a few versions back and you don't even get to the permissions screen, my guess right now would probably be a cache database migration issue. 

If you uninstall and reinstall the app, does it work? (No data is actually stored within the app, so you won't lose anything, it will just take a moment to resync the cache from Health Connect).
@vayun-mathur couldn't they just clear storage? Just seems easier.

Clearing the cache doesn't help. I also checked on a Samsung A32 running Android 13, and the same issue occurs. I tested it up to version 2.5.4. I think I may have been mistaken earlier when I said it launched; I tested it on various devices and must have confused it with a newer version of Android—it worked fine on Android 14 and 16, but there’s a problem on earlier versions.

Would you be willing to get logs? 

Seems like it may be related to API or feature usage specific to Android 14?

Oh wait how did I forget you have to install the HealthConnect app manually for Android 13 and below because it is only part of the OS in Android 14 and later.

Thanks for the logs, that confirms the issue. The app should work if you install Health Connect: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.apps.healthdata&hl=en_US

On Android 14, this app was turned into a system component of Android, so lower versions need you to manually install the app.
